 - Claude Code subagents https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents : frontmatter supports `model` (sonnet/opus/haiku/fable), `effort`, `tools`, `skills`, `memory`, `maxTurns`; "Use Haiku for Exploration" for read-only search; description should be short ("kept brief"), detailed logic goes in body; depth cap default 3, concurrency 20, env CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH / _MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS.
7. XML tags, roles, examples [P]
 - Master page still recommends XML tags ("reduces misinterpretation"), a one-sentence role ("Even a single sentence makes a difference"), 3-5 examples in <example> tags. None of this is deprecated. Note: no guidance requires a fixed N-part tag skeleton; XML is for separating instruction/context/input types.
 - Examples caveat on Fable 5.1: one complete example fixed unmarked quoting. Sonnet 5: "Positive examples... tend to be more effective than negative examples or instructions that tell the model what not to do."
 - Tell Claude what to do rather than what not to do; give the reason ("Claude is smart enough to generalize from the explanation"). Fable 5: "performs better when it understands the intent behind a request".
8. reasoning_extraction refusals: DIRECT RISK TO WISP SCHEMAS [P]
 - Fable 5, Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5: "Prompts, skills, and tool descriptions that ask the model to write out its thinking or reasoning may be declined with the reasoning_extraction category." Fix: "Ask for a short explanation of the answer or a summary of the actions taken instead", or read summarized thinking blocks. Server-side fallback does not retry these.
 - Wisp schemas carry a "reasoning scratchpad field" and agent frontmatter says "reasoning is a private scratchpad". Must be audited and reframed as `rationale`/`evidence_summary`/`actions_taken`, not "your reasoning/thinking".
9. Verbosity, format, narration [P]
 - Opus 5 longer by default; effort does not shorten visible output; prompt for length. Written deliverables also longer: "do not pad with filler sections, redundant summaries, or boilerplate".
 - Fable 5.1 formats less; "If your prompt contains anti-formatting language, remove it". Sonnet 5.5/Opus 5.5/Fable 5.1 progress text comes as thinking blocks with empty text unless display "updates". Remove "hold all findings for the final response".
 - Fable 5: "The way to keep output short is to be selective about what you include..., not to compress the writing into fragments, abbreviations, arrow chains".
10. Autonomy defaults, scope, finishing [P]
 - Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 sample: "Keep working until everything the user asked for is done, and only stop to ask when you can't go on without the user or before a risky step. When the work the user asked for is done and checked, stop and report. Don't add features, tests, files, docs or refactors that weren't asked for."
 - Fable 5.1: "The user's request... sets the scope, and the scope is the deliverable: don't quietly narrow, widen, or swap it." Unattended: "The user is not watching in real time... asking 'Want me to…?' will block the work."
 - Opus 5.5 unattended: treat text-only end_turn as a report; keep a checklist; "stop after two or three automatic continuations on the same task rather than repeating them indefinitely". This is retry-cap guidance, consistent with Wisp's cap of 3.
 - Master: balancing autonomy/safety prompt (confirm destructive/irreversible/externally visible actions) remains.
11. Context and memory [P]
 - Master: multi-window workflows: first window sets up framework (tests.json, init.sh), later windows iterate; use JSON for structured state, free text for progress notes, git for state; "consider starting with a brand new context window rather than using compaction. Claude's latest models are extremely effective at discovering state from the local filesystem."
 - Fable 5: memory = markdown notes, "Store one lesson per file with a one-line summary at the top... delete notes that turn out to be wrong."
 - Claude Code: context is the fundamental constraint; subagents for investigation; "If you've corrected Claude more than twice on the same issue... /clear".
 - Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5: keep history append-only; changing system/tools mid-session invalidates thinking blocks and cache. Relevant to any Wisp harness that edits prompts per phase: use a fresh agent per phase (which Wisp does).
12. Skills authoring [P] https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices
 - "Default assumption: Claude is already very smart. Only add context Claude doesn't already have."
 - Degrees of freedom: low freedom (exact scripts) only for "Operations are fragile and error-prone / Consistency is critical"; high freedom for heuristics. "Narrow bridge with cliffs" vs "open field".
 - Description: third person, what + when; <=1024 chars; SKILL.md body <500 lines; references one level deep; validation feedback loops ("Run validator -> fix errors -> repeat"); plan-validate-execute with machine-verifiable intermediate files for "Batch operations, destructive changes, complex validation rules, high-stakes operations".
 - Eval-driven: "Create evaluations BEFORE writing extensive documentation", >=3 evals, "Tested with Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus". Use Claude A/Claude B iteration. Gerund names suggested (Wisp deliberately uses single lifecycle words; acceptable, doc lists noun/action forms as acceptable).
 - Template strictness: "ALWAYS use this exact template" appropriate for strict data formats; flexible otherwise.
13. Frontend / design / "AI slop" [P]
 - Master (frontend_aesthetics block): "You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs... 'AI slop' aesthetic"; vary fonts/themes; "You still tend to converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example)".
 - Opus 5.5 page: "a general instruction such as 'avoid a generic AI look' mostly swaps one default for another. It responds well to instructions that name specific patterns to avoid... Work iteratively: check which styles the first result used instead, and extend the list". Sample bans: cream/off-white background, italic accent words, numbered 01/02/03 labels, monospace labels, pill buttons.
 - Sonnet 5: "Generic instructions... tend to shift the model to a different fixed palette rather than producing variety. Two approaches work reliably: 1. Specify a concrete alternative... 2. Have the model propose options before building": "propose 4 distinct visual directions... Ask the user to pick one, then implement only that direction."
 - Blog https://www.claude.com/blog/improving-frontend-design-through-skills : four vectors (typography, themes, motion, backgrounds); avoid "low-altitude hardcoded logic like specifying exact hex codes and vague high-altitude guidance" [P via fetch summary].
 - Harness blog evaluator criteria for design: design quality, originality, craft, functionality [P, summarized].
 - Claude Design (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design) is linked from master page as a canvas for interactive design iteration [S: link only, page not fetched].

## C. Per-model quick table (for tiering) [P]
- Haiku 5.5: default medium, thinking on by default, 128k max_tokens, can disable thinking at <=high. low: skips search/stops early/skips checks in long agent prompts. Compare against Sonnet 5.5 at xhigh/max.
- Sonnet 5.5: default high; for agentic coding start medium (well-specified) -> high. Self-reported tendency to add tests/docs unprompted; verifies less at low.
- Opus 5.5: default medium; medium >= Opus 5 high; xhigh/max only where measured. Thinks more per turn than Opus 5 at same level. Better code review ("more bugs caught... fewer false alarms").
- Fable 5.1: default high; low is "often competitive with Claude Opus and Claude Sonnet models on cost per task while scoring higher". Strongest long-horizon; "Longer turns by default" (minutes to hours).

## D. Assessment of Wisp practices

### Still right (keep)
1. Separate scanner/recon (recall, enumerate) from adversary/gate (filter, judge). Directly backed by Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 review-harness advice and harness blog generator/evaluator split. [P]
2. Gate in a fresh context from the producer; do not self-grade. [P]
3. Schema-first JSON handoffs between agents: matches skills guidance on "verifiable intermediate outputs", "plan-validate-execute", and "Use structured formats for state data". [P] Use structured outputs where available (docs: structured outputs; Sonnet 5.5 caveat: with JSON-only output the model can only reason in thinking, so keep adaptive thinking on and effort >= high or add "Think the problem through before you answer.").
4. Retry caps on gates: Opus 5.5 "stop after two or three automatic continuations"; Claude Code Stop-hook "cap on consecutive blocks". Wisp's cap of 3 is consistent. [P]
5. Progressive loading of references (one `<load_first>`), tight SKILL.md, refs one level deep: matches skills best practices. Verify no reference-of-reference chains. [P]
6. Tier by cognitive mode, with lower effort for subagents: effort doc literally lists "such as subagents" under low. [P]
7. XML sections for separating content types and a one-line role: still endorsed. [P]
8. Abstract tool language, single actionable rule per item, no time-sensitive info: consistent with skills guidance. [P]
9. Default-fail gate with concrete criteria: matches "be concrete about where the bar is rather than qualitative terms" (Sonnet 5). [P]

### Probably unnecessary (candidates to delete, after eval)
1. Byte-identical `<constitution>` copied into every agent: pure token cost on every spawn; Fable 5 says rules/guardrails should be re-evaluated; Claude Code says prune anything where "removing this would not cause mistakes". Alternative: load shared/constitution.md only at gates, or shrink to ~10 lines and enforce the rest with validators (just check) and hooks (deterministic). Needs an ablation eval. [P-derived inference]
2. `<backstory>` persona prose: one-sentence role suffices ("Even a single sentence"). Long backstories are not endorsed anywhere; flag as probably noise. [P-derived inference]
3. Explicit "verify your work" / "double-check" steps inside agents running on Opus 5.x: documented over-verification. Keep verification as an independent gate and as deterministic commands, remove self-check chatter in producers. [P]
4. "Think step by step / think carefully" style lines and step-by-step reasoning prescriptions: replace with effort setting. [P]
5. Any "do not forget / MUST / ALWAYS" repeated emphasis; reserve for 1-2 hard invariants. [P]
6. Fixed rigid 5-part structure applied to haiku recon agents that do deterministic enumeration: small tasks may only need goal + output schema. Test. [inference]

### Potentially harmful (fix first)
1. "reasoning" scratchpad fields and any agent text that tells the model to write out its reasoning: refusal risk (`reasoning_extraction`) on Fable/Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5, and not retried by fallback. Rename to `rationale` / `evidence` / `actions_taken`, cap length, and never say "show your reasoning/thinking". Highest priority. [P]
2. Qualitative filtering instructions in scanners ("only report real/high-severity/confident issues") under literal following lower recall; scanner must emit everything with confidence+severity fields and let adversary/gate filter. Wisp's scanner already says "emit every matching candidate"; audit other agents. [P]
3. EARS WHEN/IF/WHILE in prose rules: not harmful per se, but docs prefer positive framing + reason. Rules written only as "never X" with no rationale generalize worse than explained rules ("Claude is smart enough to generalize from the explanation"). EARS in output contracts is fine (precise, testable). [P-derived]
4. Gate-chaining that spawns reviewer subagents from agents: Opus 5/Sonnet 5.5 spawn more readily and gates that ask "use a subagent to verify" add cost; the harness (skill orchestrator) should own spawning, agents should state "work directly unless X". Also set depth/concurrency caps. [P]
5. Reviewer-finds-something bias: "A reviewer prompted to find gaps will usually report some, even when the work is sound" (Claude Code docs) -> default-fail gate + adversary asked to find problems can manufacture blockers and loop to retry cap. Mitigate: blockers must cite falsifiable evidence and correctness/requirement impact; allow explicit "no findings" as first-class pass. [P]
6. Same prompt tuned on one model tested on none of the others: skills guidance says test on Haiku, Sonnet, Opus; effort names are not comparable across models. Pin effort per agent and re-sweep per model generation. [P]
7. Mutating the system prompt or tool list between turns of one session (per-phase injection) breaks cache and thinking blocks: keep prompts static per agent. Wisp's one-agent-per-phase design is fine; avoid orchestrator edits mid-conversation. [P]

### Tier mapping check
- Haiku/low recon: Haiku 5.5 at low skips searches/checks in long prompts, and Anthropic suggests medium as default. Recon is deterministic enumeration with short prompts, so low may be fine, but raise to medium if recon misses files; keep prompts short ("With a short system prompt, Claude Haiku 5.5 rarely stops before the work is done"). [P]
- Sonnet/medium scanners: Sonnet 5.5 recommendation for agentic multi-step tool use is medium for well-specified tasks, high for harder. Scanner is pattern matching over bounded hazard packs: medium is consistent. [P]
- Opus/high gates: Opus 5.5 medium >= Opus 5 high. A binding gate on Opus 5.5 should start at medium and sweep up; high/xhigh only where evals show gain. Cost-saving with no quality drop is plausible. Also Fable 5.1 low is "competitive with Opus/Sonnet on cost per task while scoring higher" -> test Fable for the hardest gate (architect/exit-gate). [P]
- Claude Code subagent frontmatter supports `effort`, so tiers can be encoded natively. [P]

## E. Lightweight exploratory / sketch mode: what Anthropic guidance supports
- Anthropic itself says vague prompts are fine for exploration: "Vague prompts can be useful when you're exploring and can afford to course-correct" and "Sometimes you should skip planning and let Claude figure it out because the task is exploratory" (Claude Code best practices) [P]. Plan mode "adds overhead... If you could describe the diff in one sentence, skip the plan." [P]
- Design: Sonnet 5.5 "When the user asks for ideas, options or a plan, give them that and stop. Don't start building or changing anything until they say to go ahead." Sonnet 5 design: "propose 4 distinct visual directions... Ask the user to pick one, then implement only that direction." This is the sketch pattern [P].
- Suggested shape: no schema handoffs, no gates, one agent (or none), effort low/medium, explicit output: "sketch, not spec", hard stop before implementation, a short "what I assumed / what would need a spec" list, and a promotion path that feeds into weaver:capture-need or scribe:draft-spec. Fable 5 "Navigating ambiguity... asked to determine next steps" and scope rule ("deliverable is your assessment. Report your findings and stop") fit. Do not run default-fail gates on sketches; label output non-binding. [inference grounded in P]
- Keep a cheap deterministic guard: sketch mode may not write outside a scratch dir (hook/permission), since autonomy-with-no-gate needs reversibility ("local, reversible actions"). [P]

## F. Research gaps
1. Anthropic engineering posts NOT fetched: multi-agent research system, effective context engineering, "effective harnesses for long-running agents", writing tools for agents, equipping agents with skills (only [S] via search listing). Relevant to orchestrator-worker costs and handoff formats.
2. Claude Code docs for skills/plugins/hooks/memory pages not read in full (only best-practices and subagents' first 100k chars). Plugin manifest/agent frontmatter specifics (e.g., whether plugin agents ignore hooks/permissionMode) unverified.
3. Model cards / release blog posts and "What's new" pages for Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 not fetched; no benchmark numbers verified. Migration guide not read.
4. Claude Design support article not fetched; frontend-design SKILL.md at github.com/anthropics/claude-code not read (could be compared to muse).
5. No Anthropic guidance found on EARS or on rigid N-section agent prompts; statements about 5-part structure being unnecessary are inference, not Anthropic claims. Need an in-repo ablation (mason:evaluate) to decide constitution/backstory removal.
6. No primary evidence on Haiku 5.5 vs Haiku 4.5 for enumeration/recon accuracy; test needed. Structured-outputs doc not read (constraints on JSON schema features, e.g. additionalProperties, recursive schemas).
7. Third-party summaries (mindstudio, claudefa.st, explainx, oh-my-fable) surfaced in search were not read and are [U]; treat as non-authoritative.

Caveat: WebFetch returns small-model summaries, not verbatim pages; "quotes" below are as returned by the fetcher. [P]=fetched, [S]=search summary, [U]=unverified.

## Model lineup
- [S] GPT-6 family: Astra (Sep 3 2026), Sol and Luna (Sep 22); GPT-6.1 Sol (Sep 29, API id gpt-6.1-sol) is Codex default. https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-sol-and-luna/ (403 on fetch), https://openai.com/index/practical-guide-building-gpt-6/ (403)
- [P] https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model : model ids gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-luna. "GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol do not support `none`; use `low` instead". Responses API for tool calling with reasoning; remove temperature/top_p/top_logprobs when reasoning active; prompt_cache_retention replaced by prompt_cache_options.ttl ("30m").
- [S] Model guide (Oct 2 2026): five-part brief: outcome, context, boundaries, definition of done, handoff. Codex: start at default effort, lower for simple, raise for deep.
- [U] Earlier GPT-5.x / 5.3-Codex / 5.5 exist (Wikipedia hits only); not read.

## Prompting (API) [P] https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-guidance (fetcher summary)
- "Default to using clear, concise paragraphs... Use lists only when the information is genuinely parallel, sequential, or easier to compare"; avoid stock phrases.
- Eagerness: "When the user expresses intent to perform new work or fix an existing issue, persist until the user's intended goal is complete." Execute, don't just propose, unless clearly destructive.
- "Before asking the user clarifying questions, you should complete the work that is already authorized from context..."
- "The user's instructions take precedence over guidelines provided in a skill." Astra is more context-sensitive: state instruction hierarchy explicitly.
- "Do not write tests for reversible, low-impact changes that mirror the implementation." Broaden tests only on new failures.
- Prompting for requests like "can you..." = do the work.

## Codex docs (moved: developers.openai.com/codex/* 308-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*)
- [P] Prompting https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/prompting : optional blocks Goal, Context, Output, Boundaries; "a short prompt often works"; (via the-decoder [P-secondary]) "describe a process when the process itself matters. Otherwise, leave ... room to search"; "one or two hard rules to block unwanted behavior". Consumer-oriented, unified ChatGPT+Codex. https://the-decoder.com/openais-new-prompting-guide-tells-users-to-stop-overthinking-and-start-with-the-result/
- [P] AGENTS.md https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md : global ~/.codex/AGENTS.override.md or AGENTS.md, then git root -> cwd, concatenated root-down, closer overrides; cap 32 KiB (project_doc_max_bytes), stops adding past cap; fallback filenames configurable.
- [P] Subagents https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents : TOML files in ~/.codex/agents/ or .codex/agents/; required name, description, developer_instructions; optional model, model_reasoning_effort (low..ultra); built-ins default/worker/explorer; agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session; subagents inherit parent sandbox/approval and cannot override it; extra token cost.
- [P] Skills https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills : open agent-skills standard; SKILL.md with name+description, optional scripts/references/assets; discovered from repo/user/admin/system; explicit `$skill` or implicit by description; progressive disclosure; distribute via plugins (skills + MCP + assets). "prefer instructions over scripts unless deterministic".
- [S] Sandbox/approvals https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security : two layers, sandbox mode + approval policy; workspace-write disables network by default; cloud = isolated container, setup phase online, agent phase offline, secrets removed.
- [S] Agents SDK: April 2026 sandbox agents + model-native harness, MCP and AGENTS.md support; Responses API default; handoffs/manager patterns. (aggregator blogs; GPT-6-specific SDK guidance not found)

## Changes vs GPT-4/o-series
- Reasoning always on for Astra/Sol (no `none`); sampling params removed; Responses API required with tools+reasoning; cache API changed.
- Shift from step-by-step scripts to outcome/definition-of-done briefs; fewer, hard rules.
- Agentic by default (acts on "can you"), so restraint must be stated as boundaries.
- Skills/AGENTS.md/subagents are first-class and standardized.

## Versus Claude guidance (my inference [U-as-comparison])
- OpenAI now pushes short outcome briefs and few hard rules; Claude/Wisp style is structured XML sections and explicit contracts. OpenAI says explicit user instruction beats skill text; hierarchy should be stated.
- Codex subagents are TOML, not markdown frontmatter; sandbox not per-agent overridable (Claude agents can restrict tools per agent).

## Implications for Wisp [analysis]
Carry over: schema-first JSON handoffs (use Responses structured outputs), default-fail gates, EARS in output contracts, model/effort tiers (map to gpt-6-luna/low for recon, gpt-6.1-sol medium scanners, high/ultra for exit-gate), skills with progressive disclosure, AGENTS.md as shared constitution pointer.
Need Codex wording: avoid the 5-part rigid agent bodies bloating prompts; lead with outcome/definition of done/handoff; state stop conditions and boundaries because model is eager; state hierarchy (user > skill > agent); no `none` effort; tests-only-when-risk wording matches existing risk-based verification. AGENTS.md combined 32 KiB cap: keep constitution reference short, link not inline. Agent files: generate .codex/agents/*.toml (developer_instructions); exploration/sketch mode can use `explorer`/`worker` built-ins or a luna/low custom agent; sandbox inherited so read-only enforcement must be via parent sandbox/approval config, not agent file.
Native features to use: skills (SKILL.md, $invoke), plugins for distribution, subagents with max_concurrent_threads cap, cloud tasks for long parallel work, worktrees [U: not fetched].
Sketch mode: fits "short prompt often works"; low effort + Luna; no gate; output labelled non-binding.

- No primary read of GPT-6 model guide, Sol/Luna launch, system cards (403). Verify directly in a browser.
- Frontend/design/vision-in-the-loop guidance not found (frontend-guidance URL 404); cookbook not searched.
- Codex plugin manifest format, hooks, MCP config, worktrees, cloud task docs not fetched; confirm how dist/codex layout matches current .codex-plugin spec.

## UB. Uber uSpec — blog + docs fetched [P, LLM-summarized fetch]
- Blog https://www.uber.com/us/en/blog/automate-design-specs/ ; docs https://docs.uspec.design/ ; repo https://github.com/redongreen/uSpec (ownership and license NOT verified).
- Problem: Base design system, 7 stacks (UIKit, SwiftUI, Android XML/Compose, Web React, Go, SDUI); "hundreds of spec pages that all need to stay accurate"; "When those specs fall behind, engineering builds from assumptions".
- Three layers: (1) Agent Skills = domain instruction files with validation rules and reference docs, six specialized skills (Anatomy, API, Properties, Color annotation, Structure, Screen reader; Motion from After Effects); (2) Figma Console MCP, open source, local WebSocket bridge; (3) rendering layer: script populates templates in Figma.

- Deterministic extraction: token names, variant values, component structure, parent-child, variable modes, layer hierarchy. LLM: a11y semantics classification, token mapping across states, spec organization, platform behavior from provided context.
- Hallucination control: reference libraries loaded first ("the agent doesn't guess at property names — it selects from documented APIs"), structured schemas, real-data grounding, local execution.

## UC. TanStack Intent 0.5 — https://tanstack.com/blog/intent-0.5-skills-you-can-maintain [P, summarized fetch]
- Library maintainers ship SKILL.md inside npm packages so skills version 1:1 with code. "It helps to solve the delivery problem. It doesn't, by itself, solve the maintenance problem."
- 0.5 additions: `validate` compiles fenced JS/TS examples in SKILL.md with the TypeScript compiler (missing exports, invalid options, type mismatches); `maintainer review` identifies guidance affected by source changes, tied to specific source+skill versions ("has someone checked this guidance against what changed?" not "is this file old?"); `repair --write` applies mechanical frontmatter fixes only, code changes need review; reusable GitHub checks for validation, generated-file drift, pending source reviews — surface in Actions summary, never auto-apply fixes; agent hooks use local CLI when installed. Skills "belong in the development process".

## IC. ICAO / aviation phraseology analogy [K — from author knowledge, NOT fetched; verify against ICAO Annex 10/11, Doc 4444, Doc 9432 before any normative use]
- Standard words with fixed meanings: affirm, negative, roger (received, not yes), wilco, unable, standby, say again, verify, correction, disregard; avoid "OK".
- Readback/hearback: pilot reads back safety-critical items; controller must verify and correct. A readback nobody checks is theater.
- SID/STAR: published named procedures referenced by name in the clearance; reduce workload, pre-agreed details.
- Lost-communications procedures: predefined behavior when contact is lost. Missed approach/go-around: predefined at decision altitude, not improvised.
- Pilot-in-command authority: may deviate in emergency but must declare and report afterwards.
- Urgency tiers (pan-pan/mayday) with fixed handling.
- IFR (controlled, clearance, controller responsible for separation) vs VFR with FIS/AFIS (information only, no clearances, pilot responsible); IFR can be picked up in the air and cancelled.
- Mapping proposed: sketch = VFR+FIS; promote = pick up IFR clearance; stall/timeouts = lost-comms; retry cap = missed approach; override = declared deviation; closed vocabulary + readback for gate churn. Limits: phraseology exists for noisy voice; rigidity is justified by lives at stake; needs enforcement/training; agents follow prompts so vocabulary must be short.

---

WHEN an agent is authored, its YAML frontmatter SHALL include: `name`, `role` (short display label), `model`, `effort`, and `description`.

WHEN assigning `model` and `effort`, the author SHALL apply dynamic routing based on task complexity:
- `haiku / low` — deterministic enumeration and mechanical validation (recon, formatting, line citation lookups)
- `sonnet / medium` — analysis and execution (scanning, drafting, planning, implementation, code reviews, standard exit gates)
- `opus / high` — judgment (Tier 3 cross-crate architectural boundary gates, terminal binding verdicts)
- `claude-fable-5-1 / high` — system-wide architecture modeling, auditing, or structural remediation
  - Reserve for bounded, single-invocation tasks; never gates or per-finding loops.

---

## Static Prompt Prefix Invariant

WHEN authoring agent prompts, THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain the `<constitution>` section as an identical static header — the first content after frontmatter, byte-for-byte the same across every agent in the ecosystem — to maximize prompt cache sharing.

WHEN executing shell operations, THE SYSTEM SHALL prioritize modern CLI tools (ripgrep `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `jq`, `delta`, `eza`) over legacy builtins (`grep`, `find`, `sed`, `cat`).

WHEN passing task-specific inputs (file paths, line ranges, criteria IDs, blocker arrays), THE CALLER SHALL place them strictly at the tail of the prompt after the static cache breakpoint.
---

## Sentinel Retry Caller Constraint

WHEN re-submitting an artifact to exit-gate after a fail verdict, the caller SHALL pass only the revised artifact and the prior verdict's blockers array — not the full verification report context.

IF exit-gate emits a blockers array in a fail verdict, the producing agent SHALL address only those blockers in its targeted patch.

---

## Spec Persistence

WHEN exit-gate issues a pass verdict, the scribe skill orchestrator SHALL write the spec to `<workspace_root>/docs/specs/<id>.json`, commit the file to version control, set `spec_file_path` to the workspace-relative path in the spec@1, and pass the updated spec to planner.

WHEN any agent consumes a spec@1 to make implementation or verification decisions, it SHALL read from `spec_file_path` when set — forwarding spec content through conversation context is not a substitute. Context is compressed across long sessions; the file is not.

WHEN spec_file_path is absent, agents SHALL proceed with in-context spec content and record a spec_file_unset coverage gap — graceful degradation, not a hard block.

IF the spec is written to disk but not committed to version control, it SHALL be treated as not yet persisted — an uncommitted file is invisible to a fresh checkout, a future session, and drift-checker.

## Plan Persistence

WHEN challenger issues an overall pass verdict on a plan@1, the navigator skill orchestrator SHALL write the plan to `<workspace_root>/docs/projects/<linked_spec>.json`, commit the file to version control, set `plan_file_path` to the workspace-relative path in the plan@1, and pass the updated plan to smith.

WHEN any agent consumes a plan@1 to make implementation or verification decisions, it SHALL read from `plan_file_path` when set — the same lossy-context rationale as spec_file_path applies.

## (1) CONTRADICTIONS

C-1 (Anthropic vs Anthropic, by model): Opus 5 verifies unprompted and explicit verification instructions cause over-verification (M1-28), but Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 at low/medium skip real checks and Anthropic supplies a "run a real check" paragraph (M1-29). Wisp agents mostly run on sonnet/medium, so the rule must be model-conditioned; WP-64 as drafted ("avoid over-verification in Opus producers") must be paired with WP-506.
C-2 (Anthropic internal): "do not use subagents to verify your own work" (M1-30) vs "fresh-context verifier subagents beat self-critique" (M1-31). Reconcile: orchestrator-owned independent gate yes; agent-spawned self-verification no. Matches WP-55.
C-3 (guidance vs repo): shrinking or removing the byte-identical constitution (M1-88) conflicts with ADR 006 and the Static Prompt Prefix Invariant, which exists for cache sharing. Cost benefit of removal must be measured net of cache hits; draft WP-62 does not state this.
C-4 (guidance vs repo): Opus 5.5 default medium and medium >= Opus 5 high (M1-19/20/103) vs constitution `opus / high` for gates. Fable 5.1 low competitive (M1-79) vs constitution "fable never gates".
C-5 (Anthropic vs caveman): Fable 5 says keep output short by selecting content, not by fragments or arrow chains (M1-51); caveman style is telegraphic. WP-65 must restrict to "Be concise." style, not caveman, and never on specs/handoffs.
C-6 (OpenAI vs sketch): OpenAI/Codex models persist and act on "can you..." (M2-08/12) while Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 says stop after giving ideas (M1-107). Sketch skill needs explicit boundary wording in both harnesses; enforcement via sandbox on Codex.
C-7 (draft WP vs repo): WP-70 says "TOML subagents" and M2-31 suggests generating .codex/agents/*.toml, but harness-authoring.md states TOML is host config, never a marketplace contract, with markdown role cards. Also "map tiers to GPT-6 models" conflicts with "never mechanically translate model tiers". WP-70/WP-63 text must be corrected.
C-8 (draft WP internal): WP-16 "~4 directions" vs WP-11 "~3 options". Pick one; Anthropic Sonnet 5 source says 4.
C-9 (guidance internal): Anthropic frontend blog warns against low-altitude hardcoded hex codes yet WP-31/DESIGN.md and Figma practice are token-exact. Resolve: tokens are system facts; direction/aesthetic guidance stays high-specific (named patterns), not hex lists.
C-10 (OpenAI vs Wisp style): OpenAI "few hard rules, outcome briefs" and Anthropic Fable 5 "too prescriptive" vs Wisp 290-line EARS constitution and 5-part skeleton; supported only by inference until ablation (M1-115).
C-11 (source inconsistency): X-NF2 reports Codex with "GPT-5.6 Sol" (Oct 15 JetBrains post), M2 lists GPT-6.1 Sol as Codex default (Sep 29). Either naming differs or one is wrong; resolve via WP-90.
C-12 (guidance vs repo): reasoning-extraction refusal risk vs constitution L242 mandatory `reasoning` field in every schema (M1-46). Also ADR 004 immutability forces @n+1 for 29 schemas.
C-13 (draft WP vs user): WP-12 keeps Artifacts optional; user said stop using Claude artifacts, try locally (X-U5g). WP-12 should default local and treat Artifacts as opt-in only.
C-14 (agent practice vs constitution): constitution mandates rg/fd/bat; rtk hook (global user config) rewrites shell commands; X-RT5 shows broken rewrite classes. Interplay unknown (WP-68).
C-15 (user vs repo): user wants fewer tests in exploration (X-U5a/b); repo ADR 008 dropped test-first only for features; verification mandatory elsewhere. Router (WP-18) must define which gates apply per mode.
C-16 (Anthropic vs repo): agent `description` should be short (M1-40); Wisp agent descriptions are multi-sentence routing text. Verify plugin spec before shortening (they also serve routing).

## (1) CONTRADICTIONS

C-1 (Anthropic vs Anthropic, by model): Opus 5 verifies unprompted and explicit verification instructions cause over-verification (M1-28), but Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 at low/medium skip real checks and Anthropic supplies a "run a real check" paragraph (M1-29). Wisp agents mostly run on sonnet/medium, so the rule must be model-conditioned; WP-64 as drafted ("avoid over-verification in Opus producers") must be paired with WP-506.
C-2 (Anthropic internal): "do not use subagents to verify your own work" (M1-30) vs "fresh-context verifier subagents beat self-critique" (M1-31). Reconcile: orchestrator-owned independent gate yes; agent-spawned self-verification no. Matches WP-55.
C-3 (guidance vs repo): shrinking or removing the byte-identical constitution (M1-88) conflicts with ADR 006 and the Static Prompt Prefix Invariant, which exists for cache sharing. Cost benefit of removal must be measured net of cache hits; draft WP-62 does not state this.
C-4 (guidance vs repo): Opus 5.5 default medium and medium >= Opus 5 high (M1-19/20/103) vs constitution `opus / high` for gates. Fable 5.1 low competitive (M1-79) vs constitution "fable never gates".
C-5 (Anthropic vs caveman): Fable 5 says keep output short by selecting content, not by fragments or arrow chains (M1-51); caveman style is telegraphic. WP-65 must restrict to "Be concise." style, not caveman, and never on specs/handoffs.
C-6 (OpenAI vs sketch): OpenAI/Codex models persist and act on "can you..." (M2-08/12) while Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 says stop after giving ideas (M1-107). Sketch skill needs explicit boundary wording in both harnesses; enforcement via sandbox on Codex.
C-7 (draft WP vs repo): WP-70 says "TOML subagents" and M2-31 suggests generating .codex/agents/*.toml, but harness-authoring.md states TOML is host config, never a marketplace contract, with markdown role cards. Also "map tiers to GPT-6 models" conflicts with "never mechanically translate model tiers". WP-70/WP-63 text must be corrected.
C-8 (draft WP internal): WP-16 "~4 directions" vs WP-11 "~3 options". Pick one; Anthropic Sonnet 5 source says 4.
C-9 (guidance internal): Anthropic frontend blog warns against low-altitude hardcoded hex codes yet WP-31/DESIGN.md and Figma practice are token-exact. Resolve: tokens are system facts; direction/aesthetic guidance stays high-specific (named patterns), not hex lists.
C-10 (OpenAI vs Wisp style): OpenAI "few hard rules, outcome briefs" and Anthropic Fable 5 "too prescriptive" vs Wisp 290-line EARS constitution and 5-part skeleton; supported only by inference until ablation (M1-115).
C-11 (source inconsistency): X-NF2 reports Codex with "GPT-5.6 Sol" (Oct 15 JetBrains post), M2 lists GPT-6.1 Sol as Codex default (Sep 29). Either naming differs or one is wrong; resolve via WP-90.
C-12 (guidance vs repo): reasoning-extraction refusal risk vs constitution L242 mandatory `reasoning` field in every schema (M1-46). Also ADR 004 immutability forces @n+1 for 29 schemas.
C-13 (draft WP vs user): WP-12 keeps Artifacts optional; user said stop using Claude artifacts, try locally (X-U5g). WP-12 should default local and treat Artifacts as opt-in only.
C-14 (agent practice vs constitution): constitution mandates rg/fd/bat; rtk hook (global user config) rewrites shell commands; X-RT5 shows broken rewrite classes. Interplay unknown (WP-68).
C-15 (user vs repo): user wants fewer tests in exploration (X-U5a/b); repo ADR 008 dropped test-first only for features; verification mandatory elsewhere. Router (WP-18) must define which gates apply per mode.
C-16 (Anthropic vs repo): agent `description` should be short (M1-40); Wisp agent descriptions are multi-sentence routing text. Verify plugin spec before shortening (they also serve routing).

## (1) CONTRADICTIONS

C-1 (Anthropic vs Anthropic, by model): Opus 5 verifies unprompted and explicit verification instructions cause over-verification (M1-28), but Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 at low/medium skip real checks and Anthropic supplies a "run a real check" paragraph (M1-29). Wisp agents mostly run on sonnet/medium, so the rule must be model-conditioned; WP-64 as drafted ("avoid over-verification in Opus producers") must be paired with WP-506.
C-2 (Anthropic internal): "do not use subagents to verify your own work" (M1-30) vs "fresh-context verifier subagents beat self-critique" (M1-31). Reconcile: orchestrator-owned independent gate yes; agent-spawned self-verification no. Matches WP-55.
C-3 (guidance vs repo): shrinking or removing the byte-identical constitution (M1-88) conflicts with ADR 006 and the Static Prompt Prefix Invariant, which exists for cache sharing. Cost benefit of removal must be measured net of cache hits; draft WP-62 does not state this.
C-4 (guidance vs repo): Opus 5.5 default medium and medium >= Opus 5 high (M1-19/20/103) vs constitution `opus / high` for gates. Fable 5.1 low competitive (M1-79) vs constitution "fable never gates".
C-5 (Anthropic vs caveman): Fable 5 says keep output short by selecting content, not by fragments or arrow chains (M1-51); caveman style is telegraphic. WP-65 must restrict to "Be concise." style, not caveman, and never on specs/handoffs.
C-6 (OpenAI vs sketch): OpenAI/Codex models persist and act on "can you..." (M2-08/12) while Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 says stop after giving ideas (M1-107). Sketch skill needs explicit boundary wording in both harnesses; enforcement via sandbox on Codex.
C-7 (draft WP vs repo): WP-70 says "TOML subagents" and M2-31 suggests generating .codex/agents/*.toml, but harness-authoring.md states TOML is host config, never a marketplace contract, with markdown role cards. Also "map tiers to GPT-6 models" conflicts with "never mechanically translate model tiers". WP-70/WP-63 text must be corrected.
C-8 (draft WP internal): WP-16 "~4 directions" vs WP-11 "~3 options". Pick one; Anthropic Sonnet 5 source says 4.

I proposed 18 new WPs (WP-501 to WP-518) and also used them to fill partial gaps in existing WPs. About 8 rows are marked "none needed" with a reason, for example where the repo already complies.

**Repo vs guidance conflicts (checked by grep and reading the repo):**
- **`reasoning` field:** 29 of 31 schemas carry it, and constitution L242 mandates it. This is the same field Anthropic says triggers `reasoning_extraction` refusals on Fable, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. I recommend promoting WP-61 to G0 (WP-518).
- **Codex TOML:** draft WP-70 says "TOML subagents". harness-authoring.md forbids TOML as a plugin contract and uses markdown role cards, and it says not to translate model tiers mechanically. WP-70 and WP-63 wording needs correcting (WP-510).
- **Opus gates:** the constitution puts gates on `opus/high` and bars Fable from gates. Anthropic says to start Opus 5.5 at medium and to trial Fable on the hardest gate.
- **Constitution and backstory:** the 290-line constitution, the byte-identical copy in every agent and `<backstory>` all run against Fable 5 and OpenAI "too prescriptive" advice. ADR 006 and the cache-prefix rule push back, so any ablation must measure cost net of cache hits.
- **Verification across models:** Opus over-verifies, while Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 skip real checks at low and medium. Wisp mostly runs on sonnet/medium, so the "real check" rule (WP-506) needs to be model-conditioned.
- **Artifacts:** draft WP-12 keeps Artifacts optional. The user said to stop using them and try locally.
- **Smaller internal inconsistencies:** WP-16 says "~4" directions and WP-11 says "~3". Caveman-style output conflicts with Fable's advice not to compress prose. Codex persists on "can you" while Sonnet stops after giving ideas.
- **Source discrepancy:** Netflix reports "GPT-5.6 Sol" and M2 reports "GPT-6.1 Sol" as the Codex default.

**Most important new WPs:**
- WP-518 and WP-506, covering the `reasoning` field costing and the "real check" rule above.
- WP-510, the Codex TOML policy reconciliation above.
- WP-512, deterministic guards: a scratch-dir write guard for sketch, a Stop-hook retry cap and sandbox equivalents.
- WP-514 and WP-515, an evaluation-methodology reference covering power limits and baselines, and long-context (200k) cost-cliff monitoring.
- WP-501, a re-check policy for model tiers and effort pins when a new model generation arrives.
- WP-508, adding skill and agent authoring conformance checks to `just check`.

The file lists 16 claims to verify before acting, including the refusal behaviour, the Opus and Fable effort claims, the unfetched GPT-6 pages and the ICAO terms (written from knowledge, not fetched).
